findings.claim: In October 2021 the CFTC fined Tether $41 million for untrue or misleading claims that USDT was fully backed by fiat reserves (2016 to 2019), and fined Bitfinex $1.5 million for illegal off-exchange retail trading and for breaching a 2016 CFTC order. Both orders were settled; no individual was named. No appeal or later change was found.

In February 2021 Tether and Bitfinex agreed to pay $18.5 million to settle New York’s case, stop serving New Yorkers and file quarterly reserve reports, without admitting wrongdoing. The attorney general said Tether at times held no reserves backing USDT one-to-one despite saying so, and that Bitfinex hid an apparent $850 million loss.

Two Italian-language papers report a 1995 Microsoft software case. Il Fatto Quotidiano says Devasini, accused of software piracy, agreed a patteggiamento (plea bargain) for a 100 million lire fine with Milan prosecutors; Corriere del Ticino says he was held among organisers of a large counterfeiting operation and plea-bargained a fine to avoid trial. Over 30 years old; no court record found.

Devasini is a named defendant, with Tether and Bitfinex entities, in a New York class action filed in 2019 alleging that unbacked USDT was used to inflate bitcoin prices. In 2021 the judge dismissed the racketeering claims but kept market-manipulation and antitrust claims; in February 2026 she certified narrowed classes. No liability has been decided.

In October 2025 Tether agreed to pay $299.5 million to settle the Celsius bankruptcy estate’s suit, which alleged that Tether improperly liquidated about 39,500 bitcoins pledged by Celsius in 2022 and sought about $4.3 billion. Tether had called the suit baseless; no admission of wrongdoing was reported.

Cantor Fitzgerald, led by Howard Lutnick until he became Commerce Secretary, is the main custodian of Tether’s US Treasury bills; Fortune, citing the WSJ, reported in 2024 a 5% stake in Tether. In April 2026 Senators Warren and Wyden asked whether a reported Tether loan to a trust tied to Lutnick’s children helped fund the transfer of his Cantor stake to them; no wrongdoing has been established.

In October 2026 Senator Blumenthal sought Tether records after the WSJ reported that Nxum, a firm one-third owned by White House crypto adviser Bo Hines, earned $6.3 million from a May 2025 Tether deal while he helped shape the GENIUS Act. These are allegations: Tether says outside counsel found no wrongdoing; Nxum says Hines got no Tether funds in office. Hines later became CEO of Tether U.S.

A September 2026 report by the Democrats of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, led by Senator Blumenthal (a partisan report), said 84% of 846 sanctioned Iran-linked wallets studied used USDT and that Tether repeatedly failed to freeze suspect wallets; Blumenthal urged Treasury and DOJ to investigate. Tether says USDT is no haven and it helped freeze about $550 million.

In October 2024 the Wall Street Journal reported that Manhattan federal prosecutors were investigating whether Tether breached anti-money-laundering and sanctions laws, alongside an older probe into possible bank fraud by its backers. Tether denied being under investigation; prosecutors declined to comment. No charges or closure were found as of November 2026.

In September 2025 German and Swedish police, coordinated by the European Public Prosecutor’s Office, searched Tether-controlled Northern Data and made four arrests over suspected VAT fraud above €100 million at Peak Mining, then its unit, probing whether chips were used for crypto mining, not AI. Tether and the companies deny fraud. Devasini is not reported as a suspect; no charges were reported.

L’Espresso, reporting with the ICIJ, found that Devasini became a Salvadoran citizen in early 2025, as Tether moved its group there, and that as such he pays no tax on Tether dividends. It cites a January 2026 SEC filing giving him over 50% of Tether’s voting rights; the filing notes he disclaims ownership beyond his economic interest.

In April 2025 Tether raised its stake in Adecoagro, a producer of sugar, rice, dairy and bioenergy in Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, to about 70%. Tether’s CEO says it has invested over $2 billion in energy and bitcoin mining; in 2025 it shut its Uruguay mining sites after a power dispute with the state utility, later settling unpaid bills.

It abandoned its Uruguay mining sites in 2025 after a power dispute. Emissions are not quantified here.

proposal.rationale: Legal 1 to 3: a personal fine plea-bargained in 1995 (R2 personal penalty). Two papers call it a patteggiamento; neither calls it a conviction, and no court record was found, so 4 is not supported. Unresolved 0 to 3 under R6: named defendant in the pending class action. Politics 1 to 2 under R7: company-level ties only. Social 1 to 2: company-level findings. Ecology 1 to 2: holdings now assessed (70% of an agribusiness, mining). CFTC 2021 status unchanged. No disbursed giving found.

results.comment: CFTC release: $41m Tether (June 2016 to Feb 2019, untrue or misleading reserve claims), $1.5m Bitfinex (illegal off-exchange retail trading, unregistered FCM, breach of the June 2016 order); settled; no individual named.

Rewritten: the sources differ in detail. Il Fatto (2025): 1995, accused of software piracy against Microsoft, patteggiò a 100 million lire fine with the Procura di Milano (its link to an earlier article has a slug reading 96). Corriere del Ticino (2024): 1995, held among organisers of a large counterfeiting operation against Microsoft, plea-bargained a multi-million fine to avoid trial; no city or amount. Neither names a court or calls it a conviction. Removed the unsourced framing of Milan investigators targeting a ring.

SDNY opinion and order (19 Civ. 9236, dated 23 Feb 2026, redacted version filed 6 Mar 2026) lists Devasini among the B/T Defendants; CEA and Sherman Act claims remain; class certification granted with narrowed definitions (two classes). The Block (2021): RICO claims dismissed, manipulation and antitrust claims kept. Pending, no liability decided.
The Block, 14 Oct 2025: $299.5m settlement; Celsius alleged improper liquidation of 39,542 bitcoins in 2022 and sought $4.3bn; Tether had called the suit baseless; no admission reported.
